headline: South Asia: French judges probe war crimes complaint against Israeli army in Lebanon: lawyer
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: French judges probe war crimes complaint against Israeli army in Lebanon: lawyer.
- Western Russia: "Threat to nuclear safety across Europe": Russia attacks substation critical to Khmelnytskyi Nuclear Power Plant.
- Africa: Sudan: Egypt Condemns Escalation of RSF Drone Attacks On Civilian and Vital Facilities in Sudan.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: US Air Force asks industry for new cruise missile for Ukraine.
- Military Times, just now: US Air Force asks industry for new cruise missile for Ukraine.
The U.S. Air Force is looking for contractors to mass produce the Extended Range Attack Munition for Ukraine.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Jamaican hotels challenge Booking.com over tax fee.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 14 hours ago: Jamaican hotels challenge Booking.com over tax fee.
WESTERN BUREAU: Jamaican hoteliers are challenging Booking.com’s decision to charge commissions on government taxes, warning that the November 17 implementation will increase operating costs as properties continue rebuilding after Hurricane Melissa. Jamaica Hotel and Tourist Association (JHTA) President O’Brian Heron confirmed that he met with representatives of the online booking giant on October 28, when the company promised a formal follow-up. He has also alerted the Ministry of Tourism to the industry’s concerns.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America - bottom line: Lionel Messi sends condolences to Spanish footballer who died following collision.
- Buenos Aires Herald, 5 hours ago: Lionel Messi sends condolences to Spanish footballer who died following collision.
Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest on Monday during a game in the Spanish football second division La entrada Lionel Messi sends condolences to Spanish footballer who died following collision se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.
- Buenos Aires Herald, 23 hours ago: An unusual October boom: Agricultural exports reach 25-year high.
Strong performance was driven by lower expectations of a devaluation and the war in Ukraine. What does the outlook for 2027 look like? La entrada An unusual October boom: Agricultural exports reach 25-year high se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: "Threat to nuclear safety across Europe": Russia attacks substation critical to Khmelnytskyi Nuclear Power Plant.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: "Threat to nuclear safety across Europe": Russia attacks substation critical to Khmelnytskyi Nuclear Power Plant.
Russia targeted the substation with three drones during its 3 November attack. Ukraine’s energy minister warned that the strike threatens nuclear safety across Europe.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Latvia convenes emergency UN Security Council meeting over Russian attack on Komyshuvakha.
Latvian Foreign Minister Baiba Braže called an emergency UN Security Council session after a Russian aerial bomb strike on an aid distribution site in Komyshuvakha killed dozens.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Kyiv mayor explains power and water outages following Russian strikes on capital's energy hub.
Kyiv Mayor Vitalii Klitschko has explained that emergency power outages, transport and water supply issues in the capital were caused by Russian attacks on the regional energy hub.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: One killed and five injured as Russian forces strike Kramatorsk suburb with aerial bombs – photos.
Russian forces have dropped four guided aerial bombs on the settlement of Yasnohirka, a suburb of Kramatorsk in Donetsk Oblast, killing one person and injuring five others
Southern Europe - bottom line: Clash intensifies between Tusk and Nawrocki over Poland’s top court.
- Politico Europe, just now: Clash intensifies between Tusk and Nawrocki over Poland’s top court.
Prime Minister Tusk says overhaul of Constitutional Tribunal is vital to preserve EU-aligned rule of law, while President Nawrocki accuses him of a coup.
- Politico Europe, 6 hours ago: Germany’s Merz warns Europe needs seat at the table as Trump renews Ukraine talks.
The German chancellor also called the U.S. move to invite Putin to the G20 “completely unacceptable,” saying Ukraine’s fate must not be discussed without Ukraine.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Sudan: Egypt Condemns Escalation of RSF Drone Attacks On Civilian and Vital Facilities in Sudan.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 23 hours ago: Sudan: Egypt Condemns Escalation of RSF Drone Attacks On Civilian and Vital Facilities in Sudan.
[SNA] - The Arab Republic of Egypt has condemned the escalation of drone attacks targeting civilian and vital facilities in Sudan, which have resulted in civilian casualties and strikes on infrastructure.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 14 hours ago: Sudan: Sudan Says 70 Drone Attacks Launched From Ethiopia Killed, Wounded Hundreds Over Eight Months.
[Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Sudan has accused Ethiopia of enabling drone attacks launched from its territory that killed or wounded hundreds of civilians and soldiers, saying it documented 70 attacks involving 187 one-way attack drones between 15 February and 27 October, according to a report by the army-led Transitional Sovereignty Council.
- Africanews, 8 hours ago: Ethiopia's Tigray rebels claim to have inflicted heavy losses on army.
It says it killed 500 soldiers and wounded 800 others during a counteroffensive near the historic town of Aksum on Saturday.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 9 hours ago: Tanzania: Today in History - Nyerere Declares War On Amin After Uganda Invades Tanzania.
[Nile Post] On November 2, 1978, Tanzanian President Julius Nyerere declared war on Idi Amin's regime in Uganda, setting in motion a military campaign that would culminate in the overthrow of the Ugandan leader in April 1979.
South Africa - bottom line: Malawi: 'You're Not Okay Upstairs!' Chilima Crash Inquiry Erupts As Witness and MPs Trade Insults.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 15 hours ago: Malawi: 'You're Not Okay Upstairs!' Chilima Crash Inquiry Erupts As Witness and MPs Trade Insults.

- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 15 hours ago: Malawi: 'Tribalism Is Keeping Malawi Poor' - Chithyola's Scathing Attack At Politics of Division.
[Nyasa Times] Malawi will remain trapped in a cycle of underdevelopment unless leaders stop rewarding political loyalty, tribal identity and regional affiliation ahead of competence, Opposition Leader Simplex Chithyola-Banda has warned in a stinging critique of the country's political culture.

[Nyasa Times] The Media Institute of Southern Africa (MISA) Malawi has accused the state of fuelling a culture of impunity that leaves journalists exposed to violence, intimidation and threats.

- Jerusalem Post, just now: Israel warns US that Iran may use chemical weapons, but Washington questions intelligence - report.
Israeli intelligence officials told their American counterparts that they believe Iran is rapidly advancing technology that would allow it to mount chemical weapons on missiles.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: Darfur survivors vow to tell story of those killed after Sudan camp attacks.
Survivors of attacks on displacement camps in Darfur recall the lives they built, and violence that forced them to flee.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: Russian strikes on Dnipro kill two, injure 20 others.
Russian strikes on Dnipro damaged residential areas and several medical facilities.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 6 hours ago: Very cold war: Who’s attacking Europe’s supermarket freezers?.
Cold stores in supermarkets across Europe have been targeted in a cyberattack with no clear culprit.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: French judges probe war crimes complaint against Israeli army in Lebanon: lawyer.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 9 hours ago: French judges probe war crimes complaint against Israeli army in Lebanon: lawyer.
France has opened a judicial investigation into a war crimes complaint over an Israeli strike on a residential building in Lebanon, a lawyer told AFP on Tuesday. French-Lebanese artist Ali Cherri, whose parents were killed in the Beirut strike in 2024, filed the complaint as a civil party this year with the International Federation for Human Rights, Cherri’s lawyer Clemence Bectarte explained. The crimes against humanity unit of the Paris Judicial Court has appointed two investigating judges to the case, she added, hailing the move as “a first”.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 15 hours ago: US signals progress in Iran talks to avert flare-up.
US President Donald Trump signaled progress on Tuesday in talks with Iran to avoid a return to war, as Tehran reported “intensive” exchanges while offering to reopen the Strait of Hormuz under strict conditions. The fresh diplomatic signals came ahead of US midterm elections on Tuesday, in which Trump’s Republican Party is pushing to retain control of Congress, faced with voter dissatisfaction over the conflict and the soaring fuel prices it has triggered. A deal with Tehran “could happen,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: Binance reveals hackers used fake job interviews, malicious code in $6.3bn heist.
Binance released on Tuesday a detailed investigation into the $6.3 billion hack of its cryptocurrency platform, showing how attackers used fake job interviews and malicious code to steal the funds. The crypto exchange said it had replenished 98 per cent of the affected assets by drawing on its own funds, with the remaining amount involving little-traded currencies that are harder to acquire. The attack, carried out over about four hours on Oct 29, was attributed by the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) to North Korea-affiliated hackers.
- The Hindu - International, 14 hours ago: Russia-Ukraine war: Strikes on a school by Russia kills 26, derailing hopes of progress toward peace.
Russia resumed its strikes on the southern region of Kherson after the end of a ceasefire in the area, the longest truce in the war raging between the neighbours since Russia’s 2022 invasion, Kyiv said

- South China Morning Post - China, 12 hours ago: 2 Pakistani police officers guarding polio workers killed by suspected militants.
Suspected militants riding a motorcycle shot and killed two police officers assigned to protect polio workers during a door-to-door vaccination campaign on Tuesday in northwestern Pakistan, officials said. The drive-by shooting in Mohmand, a district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province that borders Afghanistan, also wounded a third officer. The police officers were travelling to a nearby village to guard vaccination teams when they came under fire, police officer Ayaz Khan said. The attackers fled...

A People’s Liberation Army air defence unit has for the first time intercepted two new types of missile simultaneously during a drill – including one that made a sudden change of direction, according to state television. The CCTV report on Monday said it was a rapid response operation by the ground-based Shenwei Missile Battalion – under the PLA Central Theatre Command Air Force – which is equipped with Hongqing surface-to-air missiles. It did not disclose the type of missiles intercepted or any...
- South China Morning Post - China, one hour ago: Fake bomb threats on flights and cruise ship cause travel disruption in Europe.
At least seven flights and a cruise ⁠ship in Europe received bomb threats on ⁠Tuesday, causing disruption at airports although no devices were discovered. At least ⁠two flights to Warsaw, two to Sofia, two to Rome and one to Murcia airport in Spain were subjected to the threats on Tuesday, and another flight to Sofia had been threatened a day earlier. An airport in Warsaw was briefly shut, and the Italian Air Force accompanied one of the flights to Rome while an Israel-bound cruise ship was...

- NK News, 13 hours ago: Call of Duty’s North Korean invasion scenario hits a nerve in the South.

North Korea’s relatively strong economic growth in recent years is a temporary phenomenon driven heavily by military production related to Russia’s war in Ukraine, according to a new analysis, warning that living standards could suffer once wartime demand wanes. A recent report by the Institute for National Security Strategy (INSS), a think tank affiliated with […]

India - bottom line: Russia gives its drones bigger antennas to beat Ukraine's jamming.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: Russia gives its drones bigger antennas to beat Ukraine's jamming.
Russia is bolstering its drone attack fleet by integrating more prominent anti-jamming antennas, which are pivotal for securing satellite-navigation signals from interference. This enhancement is meant to ensure drones adhere to their pre-programmed routes amidst Ukrainian electronic warfare efforts. Reports suggest the presence of rapid jet-powered drones that quicken attack cycles.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Ranji: Ayush Doseja admits second-season blues after hitting season's first fifty.
A year on from a prolific 949-run season, Ayush Doseja has faced outside noise and a string of unfortunate dismissals in the Ranji Trophy. The Delhi batter insists his confidence remains intact, credits the Bengal attack for a valuable challenge and believes patience, consistency and an attacking style will help him convert starts into big scores and push towards India A.

Chief of Staff Major General Ali Abdollahi said Iran's military could target the material and non-material assets of its enemies, state broadcaster IRIB reported on Tuesday.

AUSTRALIA

A Victorian-style levy on short-term rentals is among a suite of proposals being put forward by the community housing industry peak body to the NSW government.

Shan Turner-Carroll wins the $50k Open Category at this year's Fisher's Ghost Art Award, an exhibition that explores everything from grief to motherhood and hope in a world that sometimes feels hopeless.
- The Guardian - Australia, 6 hours ago: For Avelima’s family, every RBA rate hike means more shifts, a stretched budget – and less time together.
Australian families feel like the goalposts are ‘constantly moving’ as they face the impact of a fifth rate rise Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Sydney mum Avelima Satiu and her husband, Chris, each work two jobs to keep their household afloat. For the couple, every interest rate rise means more shifts, less time together and a family budget stretched even thinner. “We have to review our budget; we usually look at how many extra shifts we can pick up,” Satiu says.
